speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin our assessment, how long have you been experiencing these specific symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of your symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with diplopia on vertical gaze, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. REQUEST TEST: Repeat nerve conduction study with edrophonium challenge. REQUEST TEST: Anticholinesterase antibody panel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The clinical presentation of fatigable weakness worsening with activity, improvement with rest, and vertical diplopia is classic for this condition, and the requested tests support this conclusion.
